sources.entry: Electrino - Desktop runtime for web apps using the system's browser engine. [![OSS][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/pojala/electrino) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Electrino is an experimental desktop runtime that runs web-technology apps on the system's own browser engine, aiming to be a much smaller alternative to Electron.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Electrino as a featherweight alternative to Electron that implements a small subset of Electron's APIs. It states that a "Hello World" app is about 167 kB with Electrino versus 115 MB with Electron. The currently supported API implementations are app, BrowserWindow, ipcMain, Tray, and nativeImage. The contribution checklist marks WebView integration as done, while require() support and a Node.js backend are still open. The README also includes a roadmap to target small menu bar and desktop utility apps, starting with mapping the APIs used by the Stretchly app. It lists two contacts for the project.
use_cases: build a small desktop app from web technologies
menu bar app with web UI
shrink an Electron app's download size
desktop utility running in the background
prototype a lightweight Electron-style app on macOS or Windows
notable: Output app size is tiny: the README cites 167 kB for a Hello World app versus 115 MB with Electron
Implements a minimal subset of Electron's APIs: app, BrowserWindow, ipcMain, Tray, nativeImage
Uses the operating system's own browser engine instead of bundling Chromium
Roadmap targets small menu bar and desktop utility apps rather than large productivity apps
caveats: Experimental and described as still young
Limited to macOS and Windows 10 according to the comparison table
Does not yet support require() calls or a Node.js backend
Only a small portion of Electron's API is implemented
